records.evidence_job: Practice breaking down one coherent free-response-style physics situation; interpret the shared representation, use an earlier conclusion in a later part, and make or justify a model/plan choice.
records.student_action: Interpret the shared stimulus, carry evidence forward between connected parts, and justify a physics plan/model choice.
records.student_text:
The scaffold diagram shows upward support forces and downward forces on a system in equilibrium. Use the same scaffold for all parts.
(a) Identify the directions of the forces that must balance for vertical equilibrium.
(b) State the equilibrium relationship for the vertical forces.
(c) Suppose the total downward force is 900 N and the left support provides 350 N upward. Use part (b) to determine the right support force.
(d) Could the scaffold move horizontally at constant speed and still be in mechanical equilibrium? Justify using net force and motion.
records.student_html:
The scaffold diagram shows upward support forces and downward forces on a system in equilibrium. Use the same scaffold for all parts.

(a) Identify the directions of the forces that must balance for vertical equilibrium.

(b) State the equilibrium relationship for the vertical forces.

(c) Suppose the total downward force is 900 N and the left support provides 350 N upward. Use part (b) to determine the right support force.

(d) Could the scaffold move horizontally at constant speed and still be in mechanical equilibrium? Justify using net force and motion.
records.answer: (a) upward supports oppose downward weight/load; (b) total up = total down, ΣF_y=0; (c) 550 N up; (d) yes, if net force is zero and velocity is constant in a straight line.
records.answer_text: (a) upward supports oppose downward weight/load; (b) total up = total down, ΣF_y=0; (c) 550 N up; (d) yes, if net force is zero and velocity is constant in a straight line.
records.solution_text: Equilibrium requires the vector sum of forces to be zero. Vertically, F_left+F_right=900 N, so F_right=550 N. Equilibrium can be static or dynamic; constant straight-line velocity is compatible with zero net force.
records.solution_html: Equilibrium requires the vector sum of forces to be zero. Vertically, F_left+F_right=900 N, so F_right=550 N. Equilibrium can be static or dynamic; constant straight-line velocity is compatible with zero net force.
